title: Supabase project, schema, and migrations in CI

history.detail:
CONDITIONAL: QA1 gate 1, Sprint 2, audited at commit 741ced0 (committed, clean tree). Sprint file
re-read fresh immediately before this verdict, unchanged since it was written.

VERDICT: CONDITIONAL PASS. Two required fixes, both in app/api/health/db/route.ts.
Every stated acceptance criterion is met. The conditions are correctness defects in
the route that is this sprint's own measuring instrument, and both are small.

REQUIRED FIX 1 -- the schema-missing branch almost certainly never fires.
app/api/health/db/route.ts matches error.code === "42P01", the Postgres SQLSTATE for
undefined_table. That query does not go to Postgres directly, it goes through
PostgREST, which for a table absent from its schema cache returns PGRST205
("Could not find the table 'public.schema_migrations' in the schema cache"), not
42P01. supabase-js passes the server's code straight through, it maps nothing, so
whatever PostgREST sends is what this comparison sees. I could not prove this locally
-- no Docker on this machine, so no local stack and no real PostgREST to query -- so
treat it as high-confidence, not confirmed.

That is exactly why the fix is to match BOTH codes rather than swap one for the
other: correct under either behaviour, costs one line, and removes my uncertainty
from the equation.

    const SCHEMA_MISSING_CODES = new Set(["42P01", "PGRST205"]);
    const schemaMissing = SCHEMA_MISSING_CODES.has(error.code);

Why this is a required fix and not a note: the deploy/migration race is named in the
sprint's own Risks section, R7 exists to report that window rather than crash in it,
and this branch is the entire implementation of that reporting. As written, the one
condition it was built to detect reports status "down" with connected: false -- the
database is reachable, the schema just is not there yet, and the route says the
opposite. A branch that claims to distinguish a condition it cannot detect is worse
than not attempting the distinction, because the comment above it and the README now
assert behaviour the code does not have.

REQUIRED FIX 2 -- order the ledger by version, not applied_at.
Line 30ish: .order("applied_at", { ascending: false }).limit(1). applied_at defaults
to now(), which in Postgres is transaction start time, not statement time. Any two
migrations applied inside one transaction get byte-identical timestamps and the tie
break is arbitrary, so "the latest applied migration version" can come back as the
older of the two. version is the primary key, it is the timestamped filename, and it
sorts lexicographically in exactly the order the migration chain defines.

    .order("version", { ascending: false })

This is correct by construction rather than correct by the timestamps happening to
differ. It does not currently break GroundTruth's fourth criterion -- one migration
pushed on its own does get a later applied_at -- which is precisely why it would
survive the live test and ship wrong.

Requirements coverage, all met:
R1/R2/R3 MET. supabase CLI ^2.114.0 as a devDependency, supabase/config.toml
  committed (stock CLI defaults, local-stack ports only, no real values;
  project_id = "my_little_raccoon" is the local stack identifier, not the remote
  project ref). One timestamped migration under supabase/migrations/. Grepped the
  whole tree at 741ced0 for create/alter/drop table, create index, create policy
  outside supabase/migrations/: zero hits. R2's "working local stack" I could not
  verify -- no Docker here -- see note 3.
R4 MET, and correctly restrained. public.readings has all eight columns, event_time
  nullable, RLS enabled, and zero policies. No user_id, which the Out of Scope
  section explicitly wanted left out. The comment explaining that no-policy is the
  point, not an omission, is the right thing to leave for whoever reads this next.
R5 MET. Separate migrate job, needs: build, gated
  if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name == 'push'. supabase db
  push exits non-zero on a failed migration and the step is not guarded by
  continue-on-error, so the job fails. Secret names are exactly
  SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN / SUPABASE_DB_PASSWORD / SUPABASE_PROJECT_REF as the sprint
  file demanded.
R6 MET. Drift check runs after the push, which is the right order -- a legitimately
  new migration is not mistaken for drift. The filter
  grep -vE '^\s*(--.*)?$' correctly ignores blank and comment-only lines, and a
  non-empty remainder exits 1.
R7 MET as specified, subject to the two fixes above. Route has import "server-only"
  and export const dynamic = "force-dynamic"; the build confirms it as a dynamic
  route, so it hits the database per request rather than reporting a build-time
  snapshot. maybeSingle() means an empty ledger yields data null, not an error.
R8 MET, and verified by execution rather than by reading. Not NEXT_PUBLIC_-prefixed.
  Referenced only in lib/supabase/admin.ts, its test, .env.example and README.
  app/api/health/db/route.ts is the only importer of lib/supabase/admin, and there
  is no "use client" anywhere in the repository. Then the real check: built with
  SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY="QA1PROBESERVICEROLE" and grepped the entire .next
  output. The probe value appears nowhere in the build output at all, client bundle
  or otherwise.
R9 MET. .env.example lists all three new variables, each marked Public or SECRET,
  all empty, with the reasoning for the anon key being public spelled out. README
  covers local setup, authoring a migration, and the path to production including
  the migrate job and the drift check. Grepped the diff for JWTs, sbp_ tokens,
  connection strings with credentials and private key blocks: clean.

Verified by execution, not just reading:
- lint, typecheck, test all exit 0. 5 tests across 2 files, all with real assertions;
  the three new ones cover both failure branches of resolveAdminConfig, not just the
  happy path.
- next build exits 0. Route table shows / as static and /api/health/db as dynamic.
- Started the built app with no Supabase env at all: GET /api/health/db returns 503
  with {"status":"misconfigured","connected":false,"migrationVersion":null,...}.
  A payload, not a throw, not a 500.
- Started it again pointed at an unresolvable Supabase host: 503 with
  {"status":"down","connected":false,"migrationVersion":null,"error":"TypeError:
  fetch failed"}. Again a payload, no crash, nothing in the server log.
  The third degraded path -- reachable database, missing schema -- is the one I
  cannot exercise without Docker, and it is the one required fix 1 is about.

Notes, not conditions:
1. supabase link is given SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN but not SUPABASE_DB_PASSWORD, while
   the two steps after it get both. Supabase's own documented CI example puts the
   password on the link step too. It may well be fine, since db push carries the
   password itself, but if the first CI run fails at link with something that reads
   like an auth error, this is the first thing to try, not the secrets.
2. lib/supabase/admin.ts is not marked "server-only", and the comment explains why:
   it would break the vitest import. Defensible, and R8's substance holds -- Next
   never inlines a non-NEXT_PUBLIC_ variable into a client bundle, which the probe
   build above confirms. But the guard is currently a comment. If you want it
   mechanical, split the pure resolveAdminConfig into its own module the test
   imports, and put import "server-only" on the file that actually calls
   createClient. Not required this sprint.
3. R2's local stack (supabase start applying migrations to a local database) is
   unverified. No Docker on this machine. Somebody with Docker should run
   npx supabase db reset once before this ships and confirm the migration applies
   clean from scratch, because nothing in CI exercises that path either.
4. The schema_migrations ledger depends on every future migration remembering to
   insert its own version. That convention is documented in the README and in the
   migration header, and it is enforced by absolutely nothing. A migration that
   forgets makes /api/health/db report a stale version while the schema is actually
   current -- which is the health route lying in the specific way that makes it
   useless. Worth a CI check or a test in a later sprint. Flagging now so it is a
   known gap rather than a discovery.
5. schema_migrations is a second table this sprint creates beyond R4's readings. It
   is justified -- R7 needs a version to report over the Data API without exposing
   the CLI's internal schema -- it is documented, and it ships RLS-enabled with zero
   policies like readings does. Correct call, noting it so nobody later reads it as
   scope creep that slipped through.

Re-audit after the two fixes. Both are one-liners in a single file; keep the
re-audit proportionate to that. Nothing else in this diff needs to move.

PASS: QA1 gate 1, Sprint 2, round 2. Audited at commit a98ae8c (committed, tree clean apart
from docs/sprints/state/sprint-2.json, which is my own round-1 verdict). Sprint file
re-read fresh: byte-identical to what I audited in round 1, git diff 741ced0..HEAD
over it is empty, so this re-audit is scoped to the fix as promised.

VERDICT: PASS.

Scope of the fix: a98ae8c touches exactly one file, app/api/health/db/route.ts,
11 lines. Nothing else in the diff moved. Round 1's coverage of R1-R9 therefore
stands as recorded; only the two conditions needed re-checking.

CONDITION 1 -- schema-missing branch. FIXED, correctly.
  const SCHEMA_MISSING_CODES = new Set(["42P01", "PGRST205"]);
  const schemaMissing = SCHEMA_MISSING_CODES.has(error.code);
Matches both codes rather than swapping one for the other, which is what I asked for
and the reason I asked for it: it is right whether or not my read of PostgREST's
behaviour is exact, and I could not confirm that read locally (no Docker, so no real
PostgREST to query). The comment above the constant explains which code belongs to
which layer and why both are listed. That is the right thing to leave behind -- the
next person to touch this will otherwise delete one of them as redundant.

CONDITION 2 -- version ordering. FIXED.
  .order("version", { ascending: false })
version is the primary key and the timestamped filename, so the ordering is now
correct by construction rather than dependent on two transactions landing at
distinguishable timestamps.

Re-verified by execution at a98ae8c, not by reading the diff:
- lint, typecheck, test: all exit 0, 5 tests across 2 files. typecheck passing also
  settles that error.code is a plain string, so Set.has() is sound here rather than
  quietly accepting undefined.
- next build: exit 0. Route table still shows / static and /api/health/db dynamic,
  so force-dynamic survived the edit.
- R8 re-probed rather than assumed, since the file changed: rebuilt with
  SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY="QA1PROBESERVICEROLE" and grepped all of .next. The
  probe value appears nowhere in the build output.
- Both degraded paths re-run against the rebuilt app, confirming no regression:
  no Supabase env at all -> 503 {"status":"misconfigured","connected":false,
  "migrationVersion":null,...}; unresolvable Supabase host -> 503 {"status":"down",
  "connected":false,"migrationVersion":null,"error":"TypeError: fetch failed"}.
  Payloads, not throws, clean server logs.
- The third path -- reachable database, missing schema -- is still the one I cannot
  exercise here. It is now correct by inspection under either error code, which is
  as far as a static gate can take it. GroundTruth is where it actually gets proven.

Carried forward from round 1, unchanged, none blocking:
1. supabase link gets SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN but not SUPABASE_DB_PASSWORD, unlike the
   two steps after it. If the first CI run dies at link with something that reads
   like an auth error, this is the first thing to try, not the secrets.
2. lib/supabase/admin.ts is guarded by a comment rather than the server-only package.
   Substance holds -- the probe build proves the key never reaches the bundle.
3. R2's local stack (supabase start / db reset applying migrations from scratch) is
   still unverified. No Docker here, and nothing in CI exercises it either. Someone
   with Docker should run npx supabase db reset once before this ships.
4. The schema_migrations ledger still depends on every future migration remembering
   to insert its own version, enforced by nothing.

New, minor, for whoever next touches this file: the schema-missing predicate is now
the only untested logic in the route. Both fixes landed without a test because the
logic is inline in a handler that does I/O, and I am not going to demand a
supabase-js mock for an 11-line fix I asked to keep proportionate. But the cheap
version exists and matches the pattern this repo already uses twice
(getDeployedCommit, resolveAdminConfig): export a pure predicate, test it, call it
from the handler. Do that when something else brings you back here.

Cleared to ship at a98ae8c. Note for Pipeman: docs/sprints/state/sprint-2.json is
tracked and currently dirty with this verdict. Do not fold it into a new commit
before pushing -- /sprint-ship compares the commit's tree content against what I
audited, and a new tree means it refuses and this comes straight back to me.

FAIL: GroundTruth live test, Sprint 2, commit a98ae8c82c904bd7770673522fa126a0b53fcc4d. Environment: https://my-little-racoon.vercel.app, 2026-08-16 ~11:56 UTC. VERDICT: FAIL. The schema is not in production. One root cause, and it is a credentials problem, not a code defect. ROOT CAUSE -- CI's migrate job failed, so no migration was ever applied. GitHub Actions run 31945625005 on a98ae8c: job "build" passed in 52s, job "migrate" FAILED in 8s. Step sequence: Set up job OK, checkout OK, supabase/setup-cli OK, "Link project" FAILED, and "Push migrations" and "Check for schema drift" never ran (skipped, not passed). Failing step log, verbatim, from `gh run view 31945625005 --log-failed`: supabase link --project-ref "***" Authorization failed for the access token and project ref pair: {"message":"Your account does not have the necessary privileges to access this endpoint. For more details, refer to our documentation https://supabase.com/docs/guides/platform/access-control"} Process completed with exit code 1. SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN and SUPABASE_PROJECT_REF are both set -- the step ran and authenticated far enough to be rejected on privileges, rather than erroring on a missing variable. The token does not have access to that project ref. Either they are from different Supabase accounts/orgs, or the token lacks the required privilege level. R5 stated these secrets "are already set"; they are set, but not a working pair. This is the same shape of failure as Sprint 1's Vercel connection -- an account-level action sitting between Dev Team's work and my gate. CRITERION-BY-CRITERION 1. Displayed SHA has changed from Sprint 1's deployed commit 53bc88c, no manual intervention. PASS. - Live page renders, verbatim: a98ae8c - origin/main is a98ae8c82c904bd7770673522fa126a0b53fcc4d. Match, all 40 chars. - Changed from 53bc88c with no manual redeploy step by anyone. - This is Sprint 1's inherited debt, and it is now COLLECTED. The unattended deploy pipeline for CODE is proven. Master Controller's amendment to Sprint 1 was sound: the proof arrived on a deployment that was going to happen anyway. - Note for the record: Vercel deployed this commit even though the GitHub Actions CI run FAILED. That is expected here -- Vercel builds from the git push directly and CI does not gate it, which Sprint 1's README documents honestly. Worth knowing that a red CI does not stop a deploy in this setup. 2. /api/health/db reports the database as connected. QUALIFIED, and I will not score it a clean pass. - GET https://my-little-racoon.vercel.app/api/health/db -> HTTP/2 503, content-type application/json, x-vercel-cache: MISS, x-vercel-id iad1::iad1::rjkfs-1786881377659-b8605c71be18 - Body, verbatim: {"status":"schema_missing","connected":true, "migrationVersion":null,"error":"Could not find the table 'public.schema_migrations' in the schema cache"} - "connected":true is TRUE and meaningful: the route reached Supabase, authenticated, and received a real PostgREST schema-cache error back. Network and credentials from the app to the database are genuinely working. - But the endpoint returns 503 and status "schema_missing". Reporting the database as reachable-but-empty is not the same as reporting it healthy, and scoring this criterion PASS in isolation would paper over criterion 3. - The route's own behaviour is CORRECT and satisfies R7: it returned a structured status payload instead of throwing a 500 on an absent schema. That is the error handling working exactly as specified. The route is not the bug. Do not "fix" it. 3. Reported migration version matches the newest file in supabase/migrations/. FAIL. This is the failing criterion. - Reported: "migrationVersion":null - Newest (and only) migration file, on origin/main and locally: supabase/migrations/20260815221042_create_readings.sql - null != 20260815221042. The readings table and the version-tracking table do not exist in the production database at all. - Direct consequence of the root cause above. Nothing was ever pushed to the remote database. 4. A trivial second migration, committed and pushed, changes the reported version with no manual database work. NOT TESTED -- blocked, and blocked twice over. - Only one migration exists on origin/main (git ls-tree -r origin/main -- supabase/migrations/ returns exactly one file). There is no second migration to observe. - Even if one existed, criterion 3 must pass first: a version that is null cannot be observed changing to a different value in any meaningful way. - I cannot manufacture this. GroundTruth does not write migrations and does not push. This is the criterion the sprint file names as "the sprint's actual proof", and it remains unproven for the second sprint running. THINGS I CHECKED THAT ARE CLEAN - Service role key not in the client bundle. Fetched the home page and all 6 JS chunks it references from production and grepped: 0 hits for SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY or service_role. No JWT-shaped string in any client asset either. This is R8's boundary holding in the actually-served bundle, not just in the diff. Beyond my listed criteria; recording it because a leaked service role key is the one failure here that could not be walked back. - No Supabase URL or anon key in the client bundle either, which is consistent with nothing client-side touching Supabase yet this sprint. ONE OBSERVATION, NON-BLOCKING, FOR QA1 NOT ME The migration creates public.schema_migrations itself, and the health route queries public.schema_migrations. Those are consistent, so this is NOT a second defect -- I checked specifically because the error text made a wrong-schema bug look plausible, and it is not one. Flagging only that the version this endpoint reports comes from a table the repo maintains by hand, not from Supabase's own supabase_migrations.schema_migrations tracking. QA1 passed it; it is a design question for whoever owns the migration chain, not a live failure. WHAT MUST HAPPEN BEFORE I CAN RE-TEST 1. Fix the credential pair. SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN must be a token with privileges on the project SUPABASE_PROJECT_REF points to. This is an account action by the user, not Dev Team code. No amount of re-shipping the current code changes this outcome. 2. Re-run CI (or push) and confirm the "migrate" job's Link project, Push migrations, and Check for schema drift steps all pass. If Link project fails again, stop there -- everything downstream is noise. 3. Author and push the trivial second migration criterion 4 requires. Plan it deliberately this time. Sprint 1's version of this criterion was deferred to Sprint 2 rather than manufactured; if Sprint 2's is also deferred, the "schema deploys itself" claim will have been asserted twice and demonstrated zero times. Then re-ship and I re-test all four criteria from scratch. TOOLING CAVEAT: no Playwright MCP or Chrome extension in this session. All checks are curl over HTTPS against production, plus the gh CLI for CI run state. The page is statically prerendered so the SHA check is sound. I did not render in a real browser, observe layout, or check client-side JS errors, and I am not claiming those.

PASS: GroundTruth live test round 2, Sprint 2, commit 389040cddccdb7f9c55d8f98d4065ea05f153351. Environment: https://my-little-racoon.vercel.app, 2026-08-16 ~13:00 UTC. VERDICT: PASS. All four live criteria verified, including the one that has been deferred since Sprint 1. One security claim I could not verify live is named at the bottom -- it is outside these four criteria and belongs to Sprint 4, but it should not be forgotten. 1. Displayed SHA has changed from Sprint 1's deployed commit 53bc88c, no manual intervention. PASS. - Live page renders, verbatim: 389040c - Matches origin/main exactly, all 40 chars. Changed from 53bc88c, and also from a98ae8c, so two unattended redeploys are now on the record. 2. /api/health/db reports the database as connected. PASS. - GET https://my-little-racoon.vercel.app/api/health/db -> HTTP/2 200 (was 503), content-type application/json, x-vercel-cache MISS. - Body, verbatim: {"status":"ok","connected":true,"migrationVersion": "20260816125144_grant_default_data_api_privileges"} - status is now "ok", not "schema_missing". The error field is gone. 3. Reported migration version matches the newest file in supabase/migrations/. PASS. - Reported: "20260816125144_grant_default_data_api_privileges" - Newest file on origin/main: supabase/migrations/20260816125144_grant_default_data_api_privileges.sql - Exact match on the version string. - Consistency: 3 cache-busted calls returned byte-identical payloads. Stable. 4. A trivial second migration, committed and pushed, changes the reported version with no manual database work. PASS. This is the criterion the sprint file names as "the sprint's actual proof", and it is the one that was deferred out of Sprint 1 into this sprint. It is now DEMONSTRATED, not asserted. I did not take this from Pipeman's report. I checked whether the two migrations were applied in one shot to an empty database -- which would prove only that migrations apply, not that a later push evolves an existing schema -- or in two genuinely separate steps. It was two steps. CI receipts: Run 31945625005 on a98ae8c, 12:45:53Z, "Push migrations", verbatim: Do you want to push these migrations to the remote database? - 20260815221042_create_readings.sql Applying migration 20260815221042_create_readings.sql... That commit's tree contained exactly one migration file. Production schema stood at 20260815221042 after this run. (This run then FAILED at the drift check, which is what produced the second migration.) Run 31948345639 on 389040c, 12:55:54Z, "Push migrations", verbatim: Do you want to push these migrations to the remote database? - 20260816125144_grant_default_data_api_privileges.sql Applying migration 20260816125144_grant_default_data_api_privileges.sql... Only the NEW migration was applied. The first was not re-applied, which means the remote already had it recorded as applied. So an existing production schema was evolved by a subsequent push, with no manual database work by anyone. That is the claim this sprint exists to make, and it is now backed by two separate CI runs applying two different migrations ten minutes apart. ADVERSARIAL AND SECURITY CHECKS BEYOND THE FOUR CRITERIA - Unauthenticated Data API access to the new table: GET https://rzlojpwlhbcfzpohbwso.supabase.co/rest/v1/readings?select=* -> 401, body verbatim: {"message":"No API key found in request","hint":"No `apikey` request header or url param was found."} The table is not reachable without a key. - Service role key in the client bundle: fetched the production home page and every JS chunk it references, grepped for service_role, SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, and any JWT-shaped string. 0 hits. R8's boundary holds in the actually-served bundle on this deploy, not just in the diff. - Health endpoint stable across repeated calls, no flapping between ok and schema_missing. THE ONE THING I COULD NOT VERIFY LIVE -- flagging deliberately. The reshipped migration 20260816125144 grants anon and authenticated full DELETE/INSERT/SELECT/UPDATE on public.readings and public.schema_migrations. Its safety rests entirely on RLS being enabled with zero policies, which makes those grants inert -- a GRANT without a permissive policy is necessary but not sufficient. The enable-RLS statements are in migration 20260815221042, which QA1 did audit, and the migration's own header documents the reasoning and states the statements were copied verbatim from `supabase db diff --linked` rather than hand-written. I am taking that on the SQL, not on observation. To verify deny-all as the anon role I need the anon key, which is public by design but is not in the client bundle (nothing client-side touches Supabase this sprint) and is not in the repository. My 401 above proves the API gateway requires a key; it does NOT prove RLS blocks a request that carries a valid anon key. This is not one of Sprint 2's four live criteria, and Sprint 4 owns RLS policies and the tests that prove them, so it does not gate this PASS. But note the sequencing risk: Sprint 3 adds authentication, which means real anon and authenticated sessions start hitting a table that currently has full CRUD granted to both roles and is protected by RLS alone. Verifying deny-all with the anon key is a ten-second check and is worth doing BEFORE Sprint 3, not at Sprint 4. Hand me the anon key and I will run it. Also worth noting for whoever picks this up: this migration reached production without a QA1 audit. That is by design -- cmd_reship deliberately skips the tree-hash check and my retest is the intended gate -- but the intended gate is a live test, and the one property that most needed checking here is the one a live test cannot reach without a key I do not have. Worth knowing about the design, not a defect in this sprint. TOOLING CAVEAT: no Playwright MCP or Chrome extension in this session. All checks are curl over HTTPS against production plus the gh CLI for CI evidence. The page is statically prerendered so the SHA check is sound. I did not render in a real browser, observe layout, or check client-side JS errors, and I am not claiming those.
